statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk 13% (low) after a second observed hour of the CME reopen, with NQZ26 up 0.29% at 31,151.50 on roughly 7,900 contracts and still no scoreable range, against Stress of 65% (high) as the Strait of Hormuz stays closed on Iran's seven conditions with Brent near 102 dollars and long-end Treasury yields at 24-year highs.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the mapped policy state stays EA_ON. The narrow danger window is drawn across the 13:00-15:00Z block on 5 October, 15:00-17:00 Berlin, covering the US cash open, the S&P Global services finals and the September ISM Services PMI, where the published forecast Tail path peaks at 16% on scheduled-catalyst grounds rather than on observed one-way structure. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this state.
headline: Tail edges to 13% as a second reopen hour extends the gap to +0.29% without printing a range, while flat crude and a 15.31 VIX hold Stress at 65%
body:
The CME equity-index reopen is now roughly ninety minutes old and the picture it has produced is an orderly, very thin bid rather than a price path worth protecting against. NQZ26 prints 31,151.50, up 89.75 points or 0.29% on a 31,061.75 prior close, with volume building from roughly 3,200 contracts an hour ago to roughly 7,900 now and the quoted session open, high and low still collapsed on a single level. ESZ26 is 7,787.25, up 10.00 points or 0.13% on roughly 7,600 contracts. An independent Sunday-evening futures review corroborates both levels at 31,163.25 for the Nasdaq-100 contract, up 0.33%, and 7,789.00 for the S&P 500 contract, up 0.15%, with gold 4,176.20 up 0.33% and WTI 91.02 down 0.10%.

Tail rises one point to 13%, which stays deep inside the low band. The increase reflects a second consecutive observed hour of mild upward drift, roughly 21 points added since the previous assessment, in a book that still has no scoreable reference range. One amplifier this contract recognises is genuinely present: the Nasdaq-100 is at record levels, with Friday's cash high of 31,017.53 also the 52-week high and the index up about 22% year to date, and the futures contract is now extending above Friday's futures settlement. That is the single condition of the amplifier stack that is met. There is no persistent directional efficiency to measure, no shallow-pullback sequence, no failed retracement and no repeated extension, and the move amounts to roughly 0.07% in the past hour on fewer than 8,000 contracts. A slow thin drift that has not yet been tested is not the no-retracement path Tail is designed to measure, so the step is deliberately one point rather than a band change.

Cross-assets continue to argue against escalation pricing. WTI trades 91.09 dollars, down 0.02% on a 91.11 prior close, in a real-time 90.97 to 91.85 range, and Brent is 102.25 dollars, down 0.11%. VIX remains at Friday's 15.31 close, down 6.59% from 16.39 and near its 15.30 session low, with no live update available while cash markets are shut. Federal Reserve H.15 data dated 2 October reports the 2-year Treasury at 4.78% and the 10-year at 5.24% for 1 October, both lower on the day from 4.81% and 5.17% a week earlier. Low implied volatility, a flat-to-lower crude complex and a modest equity bid is a conflicting signal set, not the aligned amplifier stack Tail requires.

Stress eases one point to 65%, holding the lower edge of the high band. The weekend repricing question that justified the 66% to 71% readings before the reopen has now been answered and the verdict was benign, which is why Stress continues to drift down. It does not fall further because the background environment is genuinely difficult rather than merely uncertain. The Strait of Hormuz remains functionally closed in the eighth month of the blockade, with Iran's parliament speaker restating that the waterway will not open until seven conditions based on the Islamabad memorandum are met and the Foreign Ministry treating reopening as its primary objective while the United States prioritises nuclear negotiations. A daily status brief as of 20:57Z records one recorded transit against an 85-per-day pre-crisis baseline, 236 vessels holding position and a crisis-pressure reading in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours. Houthi forces claimed ballistic-missile and drone strikes on an Aramco facility south of Riyadh with fires reported on Saturday, no formal production-impact figure, and fighting intensifying around Taiz, while Iraq's state oil company moved 2 million barrels through the strait. Separately, long-end Treasury yields near 24-year highs, with the 10-year above 5.3% intraday last week and the long bond at 5.69%, sit against technology earnings projected to rise more than 65% in the third quarter. That tension is a valuation headwind and a volatility source, not a mean-reversion failure mechanism.

The published forecast keeps all 24 hours in EA_ON and green. Tail holds 13% through the Tokyo handoff, decays to a 10% to 12% range across the late Asian and European sessions as depth is expected to build, ticks to 11% for the European cash open, returns to 10% through the European morning, steps to 11% into the US pre-market, then to 14% for the 13:30Z cash open and 13:45Z S&P Global services finals, and peaks at 16% for the 14:00Z September ISM Services PMI. It eases to 13% in the first post-print hour, 10% to 11% across the afternoon and power hour, 10% through the 20:00Z cash close and maintenance halt, 11% for the thin Globex reopen and 10% for the final hour. No hour reaches the WATCH band. That is the disciplined reading of this contract: a scheduled release raises Stress and uncertainty first, and Tail follows only if the post-print path actually denies retracement. The danger window is drawn narrowly across the 13:00 to 15:00Z peak.

Confidence is 86%, one point higher than the previous assessment, because the live price path is now ninety minutes old with building volume rather than half an hour old, and because the futures levels are corroborated by a second independent source. It is supported by a real-time crude quote, primary H.15 yield data, a verified Friday VIX close, verified incident and diplomacy reporting from Al Jazeera, ABC News and a daily strait status brief, and a seven-day United States calendar verified against Trading Economics. It is held below the 90% band because the equity-index futures quote carries a delayed-data label, no live VIX exists while cash markets are shut, and the session has still not produced a scoreable range. The shared Finviz context file was last collected on 29 September with a partial collection status, roughly 7,200 minutes old and far outside the 90-minute freshness rule, so it was not used as evidence; this assessment rests entirely on independently verified sources.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published hours are available from Claude history. Tail was held at 3% from 23:00Z on 3 October through 21:00Z on 4 October, mapping to EA_ON and green throughout with the dominant mode normal, because the CME equity-index complex was halted for the weekend and no Nasdaq-100 price path was scoreable. Tail then rose to 12% in the 22:00Z slot once the reopen had been observed. Stress climbed from 71% at 23:00Z on 3 October to a 79% ceiling at 09:00Z on 4 October as the weekend Hormuz, Yemen and Saudi incident flow accumulated, eased through the 73%, 70%, 68%, 66% and 64% readings of the European and US-equivalent hours, rebuilt into a 66% to 71% band across the Sunday evening ahead of the reopen, and settled at 66% once the repricing proved benign. Confidence ran between 83% and 88%, improving through the Sunday hours as current levels, yields, oil and the forward calendar were re-verified while the live price path stayed structurally unavailable inside the halt.
outlookSummary: The current hour contains a second observed hour of the reopen, which has extended the gap to 0.29% on roughly 7,900 contracts without printing a scoreable range, so Tail edges to 13% while Stress eases to 65% on flat crude, a 102 dollar Brent and an unchanged 15.31 VIX. Tail holds 13% through the Tokyo handoff, where a thin tape remains the main channel for unopposed extension, then decays to a 10% to 12% range once Asian and European depth is expected to establish two-way trade. It ticks to 11% for the 07:00Z European cash open as a liquidity-transition allowance, returns to 10% through the European morning, and rebuilds to 11% into the US pre-market. It steps to 14% for the 13:30Z cash open and 13:45Z S&P Global services finals and peaks at 16% for the 14:00Z September ISM Services PMI, which the narrow 13:00 to 15:00Z danger window covers. That step is a scheduled-catalyst reading rather than observed one-way structure, and an orderly two-way reaction would invalidate it, while a failed-retracement sequence after the print would argue for holding the peak. Tail then eases to 13%, 10% to 11% across the afternoon and power hour, 10% through the 20:00Z cash close and the CME maintenance halt, 11% for the thin Globex reopen and 10% for the final hour. Stress trends from 65% down to 59% by the end of the horizon and Confidence eases from 86% to 75% as distance from this assessment's evidence cutoff grows. Every published hour maps to EA_ON and green.
